section_summary: This section contains a 1944 Embassy despatch reporting that Japan’s official Dōmei news magazine serialized Lin Yu-t’ang’s Between Tears and Laughter as anti-American and anti-British propaganda. It also includes a 1941 Department of State memorandum summarizing military-intelligence biographical reports on Japanese generals Raishirō Sumita, Kenji Doihara, and Gen Sugiyama.

subfiles.title: Publication in Japan of Lin Yu-t'ang’s “Between Tears and Laughter”
subfiles.from: Edward E. Rice, Second Secretary of Embassy, Sian
subfiles.to: The Secretary of State, Washington, D.C.
subfiles.about: Reports the Japanese serialization and propaganda use of Lin Yu-t'ang’s Between Tears and Laughter.
subfiles.summary: Rice reports that the official Dōmei News Agency magazine Dōmei Sekai Shūhō published installments of a Japanese translation of Between Tears and Laughter in its March 11 and April 1, 1944 issues. He concludes that Japanese authorities regarded Lin Yu-t'ang’s book as useful anti-American and anti-British propaganda. He also recalls that Lin had traveled to the United States on an official Chinese passport and received an official visa at the Chinese Foreign Office’s insistence.

subfiles.title: Outline Biographies of Japanese Generals Reported by M.I.D.
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: Summarizes M.I.D. reports concerning the recent appointments of three senior Japanese Army officers.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum abstracts M.I.D. reports nos. 10218–10220 of October 15, 1940, from Tokyo. It identifies Major General Raishirō Sumita as head of the inspectorate regulating traffic from French Indochina into China, Lieutenant General Kenji Doihara as an appointee to the Supreme Military Council, and General Gen Sugiyama as Chief of the General Staff.
